verses.text: Elijah the Tishbite, one of the settlers of Gilead, told Ahab, “As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel I serve, lives, there will be no dew or rain in the coming years until I give the word.”
Then the LORD gave Elijah this message:
“Leave here, go east, and hide beside the Cherith stream near the Jordan.
You'll drink from the stream. I've ordered the ravens to feed you there.”
Elijah did what the LORD told him. He went and lived beside the Cherith stream near the Jordan.
The ravens brought him bread and meat in the morning and again in the evening, and he drank from the stream.
After a while the stream dried up because no rain had fallen in the land.
Then the LORD gave him another message:
“Get up, go to Zarephath in Sidon, and stay there. I've commanded a widow there to provide for you.”
So Elijah went to Zarephath. When he reached the city gate, he found a widow gathering sticks. He called to her, “Please bring me a little water to drink in a jar.”
As she went to get it, he called after her, “Please bring me a bite of bread too.”

She replied, “As surely as the LORD your God lives, I have nothing baked. There's just a handful of flour in a jar and a little oil in another jar. I'm gathering a couple of sticks so I can go home and make one last meal for my son and me. Then we'll eat it and die.”
Elijah said to her, “Don't be afraid. Go ahead and do what you said. Just make me a small loaf first and bring it out to me. Then make some for yourself and your son.
Because this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: ‘The flour in the jar won't run out, and the oil in the jar won't run dry until the day the LORD sends rain on the land.’”
She went and did what Elijah said. She, Elijah, and her household had food for many days.
The flour never ran out, and the oil never ran dry, just as the LORD had promised through Elijah.
Later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick. He grew so ill that he stopped breathing.
The woman said to Elijah, “What do you have against me, man of God? Did you come here to bring up my sin and kill my son?”
“Give me your son,” Elijah said. He took him from her arms, carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying, and laid him on his bed.
He cried out to the LORD, “LORD my God, have you brought disaster even on the widow I'm staying with by taking her son's life?”
He stretched himself over the child three times and cried out to the LORD, “LORD my God, please let this child's life come back into him.”
The LORD listened to Elijah. The child's life returned, and he came back to life.
Elijah carried the child downstairs from his room and gave him back to his mother. “Look,” he said, “your son is alive.”
The woman told Elijah, “Now I know you're a man of God and that the LORD's word you speak is true.”
